candidate.answerReason: The four triangles formed by the diagonals have areas 18, 24, 32, and 24, totaling 98 and matching D.

methods.label: Use similar triangles
methods.explanation:
Write \([XYZ]\) for the area of \(\triangle XYZ\). The parallel bases suggest comparing \(\triangle ABK\) and \(\triangle CDK\): they have equal vertical angles at \(K\) and equal alternate interior angles because \(AB\parallel CD\). They are therefore similar, with corresponding side ratio
\[
\frac{AK}{CK}=\frac{BK}{DK}=\frac{AB}{CD}=\frac34.
\]
These ratios let us recover the other three triangular areas from \([AKD]=24\). Triangles with bases on the same line and the same opposite vertex have a common altitude, so their areas are proportional to their bases. Using bases on \(BD\),
\[
[ABK]=\frac{BK}{DK}[AKD]=\frac34\cdot24=18.
\]
Using bases on \(AC\),
\[
[CKD]=\frac{CK}{AK}[AKD]=\frac43\cdot24=32,
\]
and
\[
[BKC]=\frac{CK}{AK}[ABK]=\frac43\cdot18=24.
\]
The diagonals divide the trapezoid into these four triangles with disjoint interiors. Its area is consequently
\[
18+24+32+24=\boxed{98},
\]
choice \(\text{D}\).
methods.levelReason: AA similarity and common-altitude triangle area ratios are standard AMC 10 geometry.

methods.label: Compare triangle heights through their areas
methods.explanation:
Write \([XYZ]\) for the area of \(\triangle XYZ\), and let \(h>0\) be the perpendicular distance between the parallel bases. Then
\[
[ABD]=\frac{9h}{2},\qquad [CBD]=\frac{12h}{2}.
\]
These triangles share base \(BD\), so the perpendicular distances from \(A\) and \(C\) to line \(BD\) are in the ratio \(3:4\). The same height ratio applies when their common base is shortened to either \(DK\) or \(BK\). Hence
\[
\frac{[AKD]}{[CKD]}=
\frac{[AKB]}{[CKB]}=\frac34.
\]
Since \([AKD]=24\), this gives \([CKD]=32\).

Also, \(\triangle ABD\) and \(\triangle ABC\) share base \(AB\) and have the same altitude \(h\), so their areas are equal. Subtracting their common triangle \(ABK\) gives \([AKD]=[BKC]=24\). The second ratio above now gives \([ABK]=\frac34\cdot24=18\).

Adding the four nonoverlapping triangular areas gives
\[
[ABCD]=18+24+32+24=\boxed{98},
\]
choice \(\text{D}\).
methods.levelReason: This alternative uses only base-times-height triangle areas, proportionality, and addition and subtraction of areas.
